analysis:
Both changed files are CI test scripts for the threat-review scanner (.github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py, test-threat-diagnostics.py). They contain no provider runtime, coordinator, cryptographic or cache-storage code. Because of that, none of the provider assets or boundaries in the canonical model (A-001..A-017, TB-002/003/007/009/010/011, T-041) are touched by the change.

The head-side edits add tests, and none of them weaken a control:
- Manual GitHub rerun hands off without paid work: asserts MANUAL_SCAN_RERUN_DISABLED, no model calls, and clean() false (test-threat-budget.py ~950-959).
- Scanner runtime bounds (900s default, 60..3000s accepted) and invalid values rejected (~961-967).
- Bedrock workload ceiling hands off at the exact unadmitted stage with no clearance (~969-982).
- test-threat-diagnostics.py lines 186-187 and 196 add plan_calls assertions to the multi-tier integration test, checking that call planning is invoked per reduction tier ([2, 1]).

The tests assert fail-closed behavior: clean() stays false on incomplete reviews, repairs share a single allowance, and diagnostics exclude private response text. No secrets are introduced. Only synthetic tokens appear, such as GH_TOKEN="synthetic".

The production scanner changes (threat_review modules, runtime_seconds, the BEDROCK_SCAN_CALL_POLICY workload policy, plan_calls) are not in the supplied units, so I could not verify that they implement what the tests assert. This is a coverage limit rather than a finding. No regression is identified in the supplied evidence.
